title: Dhuska with Chana Dal
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.
recipe: Soak rice and chana dal, grind into a slightly coarse batter with green chilli, ginger and salt. Ferment briefly if desired.
Heat oil and deep-fry spoonfuls of batter into thick, golden, crispy discs.
Serve hot with ghugni, potato curry or chutney.
tips: Iconic Jharkhand breakfast and street snack – crisp outside, soft inside.
Best eaten fresh from the oil.

jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.
recipe: Soak rice and urad dal, grind into a slightly coarse batter with green chilli, ginger and salt. Ferment briefly if desired.
Heat oil and deep-fry spoonfuls of batter into thick, golden, crispy discs.
Serve hot with ghugni, potato curry or chutney.
tips: Iconic Jharkhand breakfast and street snack made with urad dal.
Crisp outside, soft inside.

title: Chilka Roti with Chana Dal
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (rice, chana dal, salt, oil). No onion, garlic, ginger, or root vegetables.
recipe: Soak rice and chana dal overnight. Grind into a smooth batter and add salt.
Heat a tawa, grease lightly, pour and spread the batter into a thin pancake. Cook both sides till golden.
Serve with chutney, vegetable curry or meat curry.
tips: Traditional rice-and-chana dal pancake of the Chotanagpur region.
Light yet filling.

Light yet filling.

title: Litti Chokha
jainNotes: Contains onion, garlic, ginger - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Sattu, mustard oil, garlic, ginger, green chilli, ajwain, lemon, salt
Onion, green chilli, mustard oil for chokha

recipe: Prepare spiced sattu stuffing with mustard oil and aromatics. Stuff into wheat dough balls and seal.
Roast over charcoal or bake till the crust is crisp and slightly charred.
Make chokha by roasting and mashing brinjal, tomato and potato with onion, green chilli and mustard oil.
Dip hot littis in ghee and serve with chokha.
tips: Shared with Bihar but equally iconic in Jharkhand – rustic, smoky and satisfying.
Traditional open-fire roasting is ideal.

title: Rugda (Rugra) Curry
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Onion, garlic, green chilli, turmeric, salt

recipe: Clean the rugda thoroughly. Heat mustard oil, sauté onion, garlic and chilli.
Add the mushrooms, turmeric and salt. Cook till tender and well-flavoured.
Serve with rice – a seasonal forest delicacy.
tips: Wild mushroom prized in Jharkhand tribal cuisine – available mainly in the monsoon/early winter.
Simple preparation highlights the natural flavour.

title: Ghugni with Black Chickpeas
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and ginger.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

recipe: Pressure-cook the soaked black chickpeas. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with mustard oil.
Add the chickpeas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot, often with muri (puffed rice) or as a side.
tips: Everyday protein-rich curry made with black chickpeas.
Often eaten with puffed rice as muri-ghugni.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

recipe: Pressure-cook the soaked white peas. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with mustard oil.
Add the peas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot, often with muri (puffed rice) or as a side.
tips: Everyday protein-rich curry made with white peas.
Often eaten with puffed rice as muri-ghugni.

title: Dal Pitha
jainNotes: Contains ginger and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger-garlic.

ingredients.name: Ginger, garlic, green chilli, cumin, salt

recipe: Cook and grind spiced chana dal into a filling. Make a soft rice-flour dough.
Stuff, shape into parcels and steam (often in leaves) till cooked.
Serve with green chutney or mustard dip.
tips: Steamed rice-flour dumplings with spiced dal – light and traditional winter dish.
Similar to Bihari versions but firmly part of Jharkhand home cooking.

title: Jharkhandi Mutton Curry
jainNotes: Contains mutton, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Garam masala, red chilli, turmeric, mustard oil

recipe: Marinate mutton with yogurt and spices. Sauté onion and ginger-garlic in mustard oil.
Add the mutton and cook till tender in a rich, spiced gravy.
Serve with rice or roti – common at celebrations and in non-tribal as well as tribal homes.
tips: Hearty meat curry – mustard oil gives the characteristic aroma.
Slow cooking is preferred.

title: Koinar Saag
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.

ingredients.name: Garlic, green chilli, mustard oil, salt

recipe: Wash and chop the koinar leaves. Heat mustard oil, add crushed garlic and chilli.
Add the greens and salt. Stir-fry till just wilted and flavourful.
Serve as a simple side with rice.
tips: Popular local leafy green of Jharkhand – nutritious and everyday.
Minimal cooking preserves nutrients and colour.

title: Thekua
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (wheat flour, jaggery, ghee, cardamom). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.

ingredients.name: Oil or ghee for deep frying

recipe: Melt jaggery with a little water. Mix into wheat flour with ghee and cardamom to form a stiff dough.
Shape into discs (use traditional moulds if available) and deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. Especially made for Chhath Puja.
tips: Iconic Chhath festival sweet shared with Bihar – crisp, mildly sweet and long-lasting.
Ghee in the dough improves flavour.

title: Arsa Roti
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (rice, jaggery, oil). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
recipe: Soak rice, grind into a paste. Cook jaggery into a thick syrup and mix with the rice paste.
Shape into small discs and deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. A festive sweet.
tips: Traditional rice-jaggery sweet of the region – made during festivals.
Crisp exterior with sweet interior.

title: Bhaat Dal with Toor Dal & Saag
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.

ingredients.name: Seasonal saag (greens) with garlic, green chilli, mustard oil

recipe: Cook rice and a simple tempered toor dal.
Prepare a side of seasonal saag stir-fried with garlic and green chilli in mustard oil.
Serve the everyday Jharkhandi plate of rice, dal and greens with pickle.
tips: The daily meal of most households – simple, balanced and rice-centric.
Mustard oil is the preferred cooking medium.

title: Tribal-style Pork Curry
jainNotes: Contains pork, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Cut pork into pieces. Sauté onion, garlic, ginger and chilli in mustard oil.
Add the pork and cook slowly till tender, using minimal water so the meat cooks in its own fat and juices.
Season simply. Serve with rice – common in many tribal communities.
tips: Pork is widely eaten in tribal Jharkhand – preparations are often simple and robust.
Slow cooking on low heat yields the best texture.
